chunks: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, who said: Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from whoever narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) set out, traveling with the people. When he was about a mile or two from Karbala, he advanced ahead of them until he reached the places of prostration of the martyrs. He said: 'Two hundred prophets, two hundred successors, and two hundred tribesmen were taken (as martyrs) there with their followers.' He then circled it on his she-camel, his feet out of the stirrups, and began to say: 'A resting place for camels and places of prostration for martyrs; those who came before them cannot precede them, and those who come after them cannot catch up with them.'

key_terms.مَصَارِعِ الشُّهَدَاءِ: Places of prostration of the martyrs

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the spiritual status of Karbala when he visited it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) visits Karbala, specifically the site known as 'Masa'ir al-Shuhada' (the places where the martyrs fell), and identifies it as the resting place of two hundred prophets, successors (Awsiya), and tribesmen (Asbita). He circumambulates the area on his donkey, with his feet touching the ground, and recites poetry highlighting the unique, unsurpassed status of these martyrs in Islamic history. This act underscores the Shia scholarly view of Karbala as a sacred locus of divine presence and martyrdom, linking the Ahl al-Bayt's suffering to the broader lineage of prophethood.
